chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn Musa from Muhammad ibn 'Isa from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Wassha' from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) who said:
"Every intoxicant is forbidden and every fermented drink is forbidden and al-fuqqa' (a type of fermented drink) is forbidden."

272 - Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Bakr ibn Salih from Zakariyya ibn Yahya said: I wrote to Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) asking him about al-fuqqa' and describing it to him, so he said, 'Do not drink it.' So I repeated it to him, describing to him how it is made, so he said, 'Do not drink it and do not return to me regarding it.'

key_terms.الْفُقَّاعُ: Al-fuqqa' (a specific type of fermented drink)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on al-fuqqa' and fermented drinks in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Rida (AS) establishes the principle of 'kullu muskirin haram' (every intoxicant is forbidden), extending the prohibition to 'al-fuqqa'' (a fermented drink, often identified as beer or a specific type of fermented grain beverage). The Imam's instruction 'la turaj'ini fihi' (do not revisit me regarding it) signifies a definitive, non-negotiable ruling, indicating that even if the specific preparation method is clarified, the substance remains impermissible due to its intoxicating nature or inherent quality.
